verdict.rationale: Tavily has a dedicated rate-limits page with per-environment RPM caps (Development 100, Production 1,000) and documents 429 responses with a retry-after header. The pricing page lists a no-card free tier and pay-as-you-go credits, which points to a self-serve path, though the evidence never explicitly describes upgrading or how a key moves to Production limits. Concurrency caps (as distinct from requests per minute) are not documented. missing for 10: documented concurrency caps, explicit self-serve upgrade flow tying plan or environment to higher limits, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can read documented rate limits and concurrency caps with a self-serve upgrade path
